paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God shows Ezekiel that the worst of it is not out in the open. It's behind a wall, in the dark, where the elders think nobody can see. God says they are saying, "The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land." (Ezekiel 8:12) But God asked Ezekiel, "do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness" (Ezekiel 8:12), and that tells you the dark hides nothing from Him.

Now look at who was doing all this. Elders, women at the north gate, and men in the inner court, all of them in or at the house of the LORD (Ezekiel 8:11, 14, 16). They could stand in the right building and still have their backs to Him, like the men who turned "with their backs to the temple of the LORD" (Ezekiel 8:16). Being near God's house is not the same as turning your face toward Him, and I say that as a stamper who spent years in a drawer near a kitchen and still wasn't baking!

So here's what I want you to carry, baker. God sees every hidden room, and He cares about what's in them. God said these things were done "to drive Me far from My sanctuary" (Ezekiel 8:6), and that is a heavy thing to read. Let it make you ask what you're facing toward right now, and bring even the private corners to Him. This story isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm.
